reasons: Provenance US (ADA). Green ceiling <5.4% has no guideline basis; ADA normoglycemia is <5.7%, so 5.4-5.6% normoglycemic people are mislabeled suboptimal and yellow 5.4-6.4 imperfectly overlaps ADA prediabetes 5.7-6.4. US<->UK divergence: NICE prediabetes is 6.0-6.4 (narrower than ADA 5.7-6.4), so the US-centric yellow over-flags under NICE.

The green/yellow boundary at 5.4% is invented and unsupported by the cited ADA source: ADA defines normal <5.7%, prediabetes 5.7-6.4%, diabetes >=6.5%, so 5.4-5.6% (ADA-normal) is mislabelled as caution. Provenance: US ADA. US↔UK divergence: WHO/NICE prediabetes is HbA1c 6.0-6.4% (42-47 mmol/mol) — the spec's 5.4 matches neither ADA nor WHO/NICE. Separately, all HbA1c values are NGSP % only with no IFCC mmol/mol, so UK/EU labs (which report mmol/mol) cannot use them. Raised by multiple reviewers, high severity (units gap is high).

Severity high, provenance mixed/UAE. hba1c th[5.7,6.5,'hi'] is the ADA cut and is CRITICAL in MET (floors the pillar to R_crit). US vs UK: ADA prediabetes 5.7-6.4% vs NICE/WHO 6.0-6.4% (42-47 mmol/mol) — spec runs ~0.3% stricter than UK and reports % not mmol/mol. UAE: HbA1c is unreliable with haemoglobinopathies (thalassaemia, G6PD haemolysis) prevalent in the Gulf, yet there is no haemoglobinopathy guard before it triggers the critical cascade. Confirmed by refuter.

Provenance US/ADA. ADA Standards of Care define normal <5.7% and prediabetes 5.7-6.4%; the spec's green ceiling <5.4 and yellow floor 5.4 disagree with the cited ADA source and mislabel normal 5.4-5.6% as elevated. US/UK divergence: ADA reports % (DCCT/NGSP) while UK/NHS and IFCC report mmol/mol (5.7%=39, 6.5%=48); a %-only band silently mis-parses any UK/EU/UAE mmol/mol feed. UAE note: South-Asian-heavy Gulf cohort has high diabetes prevalence and HbA1c-glucose discordance, plus haemoglobinopathy (thalassaemia/G6PD) interference common regionally that makes HbA1c unreliable.
actions: Align to ADA SoC 2024: green <5.7, yellow 5.7-6.4, red >=6.5; remove/justify the <5.4 cut.

Move the green/yellow boundary to ADA 5.7% (or explicitly document <5.4 as an aspirational optimum distinct from the diagnostic cut) and expose the WHO/NICE 6.0-6.4% divergence; add IFCC mmol/mol alongside every NGSP % value.
Reconcile ADA vs NICE prediabetes cut, add mmol/mol, and add a haemoglobinopathy guard (prefer fructosamine/fasting glucose) before HbA1c floors the pillar.
Set green <5.7, yellow 5.7-6.4 per ADA; add mmol/mol alongside % and store canonical IFCC internally; flag HbA1c unreliability in haemoglobinopathy carriers.
range:HbA1c:base.resolution: Green moved <5.4→<5.7% (39 mmol/mol) per ADA/WHO; bands carry NGSP% + IFCC mmol/mol; re-cited. Set in pillars/range-variations/calc-graph (th already 5.7,6.5) via apply_range_corrections.py.

reasons: Provenance mixed. Bands are NGSP/DCCT % only with no IFCC mmol/mol equivalent. US<->UK divergence: UK/EU labs report mmol/mol (6.5%=48; conversion mmol/mol=(%-2.15)x10.929); a UK mmol/mol feed would be grossly mis-scored. UAE note: Gulf labs follow UK convention, compounding mis-scoring risk.
actions: Add mmol/mol equivalents and a unit-locale conversion path.
rangevar:HbA1c:unit:mmol_per_mol.resolution: data/units.json: hba1c canonical SI = mmol/mol (IFCC), lin=(%−2.15)×10.929; bands 5.7/6.5 % → 39/48 mmol/mol; dual display + inbound conversion layer.

range:Systolic BP:base.item: Systolic/Diastolic BP base range vs ACC/AHA citation
reasons: Provenance US (cited ACC/AHA 2017). Citation/value contradiction: ACC/AHA 2017 defines HTN >=130/80 (Stage 1 130-139/80-89) but the spec uses >=140 red and 120-139 yellow, which is the ESC/NICE/JNC7 convention. US<->UK divergence is the crux: ACC/AHA >=130/80 vs ESC/ESH 2023 and NICE NG136 >=140/90; the chosen 140 cut is European/NICE but mis-attributed to ACC/AHA. UAE note: clinic must declare which standard it intends.

Cite/threshold mismatch: ACC/AHA 2017 (US) defines Stage-1 HTN at >=130/80, but the base bands run green 90-119 / yellow 120-139 / red >=140 — the >=140 value is the JNC7/ESC/NICE (UK/EU) threshold, not ACC/AHA. 130-139 (Stage-1 HTN under ACC/AHA) is mislabelled as mere caution. Provenance: US ACC/AHA 2017 vs ESC/ESH 2018/2023 + NICE NG136 (both >=140/90). US↔UK divergence: US >=130/80 vs UK/EU >=140/90. UAE: MoHAP/Gulf practice largely follows ESC/NICE >=140, so the number may be defensible but the citation is wrong. The <85 low-SBP floor is also uncited within ACC/AHA. Raised by 3 reviewers, high severity.

Provenance mixed/US-cited. ACC/AHA 2017 defines Stage 1 HTN at >=130/80 and Stage 2 at >=140/90; red >=140 IS Stage 2, but yellow 120-139 conflates 'Elevated' (120-129) with 'Stage 1' (130-139) -- a direct internal contradiction with the named guideline. US/UK divergence: ACC/AHA 2017 = HTN >=130/80; NICE NG136 and ESC/ESH 2023 = >=140/90, so the red cut-point follows NICE/ESH while the citation says ACC/AHA -- label and band disagree. UAE note: UAE MoH largely follows AHA; declare governing guideline and add age-stratified targets (relaxed >=80y).
actions: Reconcile: re-cite ESC/ESH 2023 or NICE NG136 for the 140/90 cut, OR keep ACC/AHA 2017 and reclassify 130-139/80-89 as Stage-1 HTN.

Either re-cite to NICE NG136 / ESC 2023 for the >=140 threshold, or move yellow to 120-129 and red to >=130 to match ACC/AHA 2017 as cited. State which standard the product adopts and source the <85 floor.

Reconcile citation with threshold: if ACC/AHA 2017, split yellow into 120-129 elevated vs 130-139 Stage 1; or change citation to ESC/ESH 2023 / NICE NG136 where >=140/90 is correct; add age-stratified targets.
range:Systolic BP:base.resolution: ≥140/90 cut re-cited from ACC/AHA (which is ≥130/80) to NICE NG136 / ESC 2023 — the convention this value actually follows and which Gulf practice adopts. Values unchanged; citation corrected via apply_range_corrections.py.

range:Diastolic BP:base.item: Diastolic BP base range vs ACC/AHA citation
reasons: Provenance US (cited ACC/AHA). DBP green 60-79 / red >=90 follows ESC/JNC, not the ACC/AHA 80 mmHg diastolic HTN cut, mirroring the systolic contradiction. US<->UK divergence: ACC/AHA >=80 vs ESC/NICE >=90. UAE note: same standard-selection ambiguity as systolic.
actions: Reconcile DBP cut with the cited guideline (ACC/AHA 80 vs ESC/NICE 90) and re-cite accordingly.
range:Diastolic BP:base.resolution: ≥140/90 cut re-cited from ACC/AHA (which is ≥130/80) to NICE NG136 / ESC 2023 — the convention this value actually follows and which Gulf practice adopts. Values unchanged; citation corrected via apply_range_corrections.py.

range:LDL-C:base.item: LDL-C base range (no very-high-risk goal; mis-cite)
reasons: Provenance US; citation_status weak. Green <100 (<70 high-risk) and red >=160 reflect outdated ATP-III framing; 2018 ACC/AHA and ESC/EAS 2019 add a very-high-risk goal <55 mg/dL that is absent, and the 'ACC/AHA' alias points to the BP guideline, not a lipid one. US<->UK divergence: ESC/EAS very-high-risk LDL <55 (1.4 mmol/L) vs NICE which uses non-HDL/>40% reduction targets rather than absolute LDL goals.

Cite/value provenance mismatch: the flat two-tier '<100 general / <70 high-risk' headline is NCEP ATP-III / US AHA framing, but the cite token is 'ESC/EAS' (European). ESC/EAS 2019 uses risk-tiered mmol/L goals (low <116 / moderate <100 / high <70 / very-high <55 = 3.0/2.6/1.8/1.4 mmol/L), not a flat <100. red >=160 maps to NCEP severe hypercholesterolaemia. Units absent — values are mg/dL but the European cite implies mmol/L, so a Gulf/UK lab reading '<55' as mmol/L is mis-scored ~38-fold. US↔UK divergence: ESC/EAS absolute mmol/L goals vs ACC/AHA 2018 %-reduction + thresholds vs NICE non-HDL / >40% reduction. UAE: regional labs report mmol/L. Multiple reviewers, high severity.

Provenance US/ACC-AHA. ACC/AHA 2018 cholesterol guideline is risk/treatment-based and sets no universal LDL goal band; green <100 / red >=160 is a legacy NCEP ATP-III construct, so the unqualified 'ACC/AHA' attribution (no year) is misleading. US/UK divergence: NICE uses non-HDL targets and QRISK rather than LDL goals; UK/EU/UAE labs report mmol/L (LDL 100 mg/dL ~ 2.6 mmol/L) so mg/dL-only band corrupts SI feeds. UAE note: store canonical SI unit with explicit unit field on ingest.
actions: Add very-high-risk goal <55 mg/dL and re-cite to 2018 ACC/AHA Cholesterol (Grundy et al.) / ESC/EAS 2019.
Either restate bands in ESC/EAS mmol/L risk tiers, or re-cite to a US source (ACC/AHA/NLA 2018) matching the mg/dL thresholds; add explicit mg/dL units plus mmol/L conversions.
Cite ACC/AHA 2018 + 2022 ECDP (risk-based >=70/<55 thresholds) with year, or relabel band source as legacy NCEP; add mmol/L SI unit.
range:LDL-C:base.resolution: Mis-cited ACC/AHA (BP-guideline alias) corrected to ESC/EAS 2019; very-high-risk goal <55 (and <70 high-risk) added to green band; engine th [100,160] retained.

reasons: Provenance EU (ESC). Single >=125 nmol/L red omits the very-high tier (~>=430 nmol/L) defined by ESC/EAS and HEART UK and oversimplifies a continuous marker. US<->UK divergence: HEART UK uses >90 raised / >200 high / >430 very-high nmol/L, differing from the spec's 75/125 cuts. UAE note: nmol/L vs mg/dL mixing risks misclassification across cohorts.

Provenance EU/ESC-EAS. EAS 2022 / ESC 2019 treat Lp(a) as risk-continuous with ~125 nmol/L (~50 mg/dL) as the commonly used actionable cut; the single high cut at >=125 is defensible but the intermediate 75-125 'grey band' is non-canonical/fabricated and should be flagged. US/UK divergence: Lp(a) is reported in both nmol/L (molar) and mg/dL (mass) which are isoform-dependent and NOT interconvertible by a fixed factor; many UK/US labs report mg/dL, so a nmol/L-only schema mis-bands mg/dL results. UAE note: capture assay reporting unit on ingest, do not auto-convert.
actions: Add a very-high tier (>=430 nmol/L); cite 2022 EAS Lp(a) consensus (Kronenberg et al.); state nmol/L assay.
Cite EAS 2022 / ESC 2019 with year; state thresholds are risk-continuous not banded; require the reporting unit (nmol/L vs mg/dL) and assay, do not auto-convert.
range:Lp(a):base.resolution: Very-high tier ≥430 nmol/L added; unit pinned to nmol/L (non-convertible); re-cited to the EAS 2022 Lp(a) consensus.

rangevar:Lp(a):unit:nmol_vs_mgdl.item: Lp(a) unit trap (nmol/L vs mg/dL non-convertible)
reasons: Provenance mixed. nmol/L and mg/dL Lp(a) are not linearly interconvertible (isoform-size dependent); the spec picks nmol/L but a US mg/dL feed would be badly mis-scored. US<->UK divergence: nmol/L preferred (UK/EU) vs legacy mg/dL (US), no safe linear conversion.
actions: Hard-reject mg/dL Lp(a) feeds or flag for isoform-aware handling; do not auto-convert.
rangevar:Lp(a):unit:nmol_vs_mgdl.resolution: data/units.json: lpa marked convertible=false (mass↔molar depends on apo(a) isoform); store native assay unit, prefer nmol/L. UI shows a 'store native' marker, never auto-converts.

range:Triglycerides:base.item: Triglycerides base range (<90 green; conflated red)
reasons: Provenance US; citation_status weak. NCEP/AHA normal TG is <150 (borderline 150-199, high 200-499, very-high >=500); the <90 green has no guideline basis, yellow 90-149 mislabels normal as suboptimal, and red '>=150 (>=500 acute)' conflates borderline-high with the pancreatitis threshold. The 'ADA/AHA' alias resolves only to ADA SoC 2024, dropping the AHA basis. US<->UK divergence: ESC/EAS and NICE accept non-fasting TG at >1.7 mmol/L (~150).

Provenance US. >=150 (elevated) and >=500 (very high/pancreatitis) are standard ATP-III/AHA, but the green ceiling <90 is stricter than the conventional normal <150 / optimal <100 and is uncited. US/UK divergence: mg/dL-only; UK/EU/UAE report mmol/L (TG 150 mg/dL ~ 1.7 mmol/L). UAE note: capture unit on ingest.
actions: Use NCEP/AHA bands (normal <150, borderline 150-199, high 200-499, very-high >=500); cite/justify or remove the <90 cut; add AHA TG source to registry.
Set green normal <150 (optimal <100) per AHA or justify/relax the <90 ceiling; add mmol/L SI unit.
range:Triglycerides:base.resolution: Invented green <90 removed → NCEP normal <150 (1.7 mmol/L); yellow 150–499 (atherogenic) separated from the ≥500 pancreatitis red; engine th [150,500] retained.

range:Waist circumference:base.item: Waist circumference base range (blended frameworks; no ethnicity cuts)
reasons: Provenance mixed/UAE. Green <94M/<80F (IDF Europid) is blended with red >=102M/>=88F (NCEP/ATP-III US), mixing two bodies; ethnicity-specific cuts absent. US<->UK divergence: US (NCEP) 102/88 vs IDF Europe 94/80 vs WHO/IDF Asian 90/80. UAE note: South-Asian-majority + high-central-adiposity Gulf Arab cohort means >=102M systematically under-flags metabolic risk; cited IDF/AHA 2009 doc supports population-specific cuts.

The base green <94 M / <80 F uses the IDF/European cut while red >=102 M / >=88 F uses the US ATP-III/AHA cut, splicing two threshold systems into one green-to-red ladder; the cited IDF/AHA 2009 harmonization explicitly keeps cuts population-specific, not as one ramp. CRITICAL for a Gulf cohort: IDF recommends South-Asian/European data for Middle-Eastern/Arab populations, so the lower (South-Asian) cut <90 M / <80 F should be the DEFAULT, not an opt-in ethnicity variation, for the large South-Asian expatriate majority and ethnic-Arab cohort. Cite tokens are also inconsistent (base 'IDF' vs ethnicity row 'WHO (ethnicity-adj)' which actually resolves to the IDF/AHA 2009 document, not WHO). Provenance: mixed/UAE. US↔UK divergence: US ATP-III 102/88, IDF Europid 94/80, IDF/NICE South-Asian 90/80; units (cm vs inches) unstated. Raised by multiple reviewers, high severity.
actions: Apply ethnicity-specific waist cuts (South Asian/Asian >=90M/>=80F) or parameterise by population per IDF/AHA 2009; document the population.

Default to the lower South-Asian/Arab cut (90 M / 80 F) for Gulf cohorts; present population-specific cuts per the cited harmonization rather than a single 94->102 ramp; unify the cite to IDF/AHA 2009 (relabel the 'WHO' token); state units (cm).
range:Waist circumference:base.resolution: European cuts (94/102) replaced with IDF South-Asian/Gulf cuts (male ≥90, female ≥80) as the cohort default; engine th [94,102]→[90,100]; re-cited IDF 2006.

reasons: Provenance intl/mixed (KDIGO 2024). Labelling 60-89 (G2) as yellow over-pathologizes normal kidneys; KDIGO 2024 requires concurrent albuminuria/damage for G2 to be CKD, endorses race-free CKD-EPI 2021, and recommends combined cr-cysC for confirmation. Splitting into two separately weighted markers (.35 cys, .15 cr) of the same construct risks double-counting and the equation is unstated. US<->UK divergence: US (NKF/ASN 2021) and KDIGO both adopted race-free CKD-EPI; older race-coefficient eGFR is deprecated.
actions: Specify CKD-EPI 2021 race-free; require albuminuria/damage for G2 abnormality; avoid double-weighting the eGFR construct (consider eGFRxUACR heatmap).
range:eGFR (creatinine):base.resolution: G2 (60–89) no longer yellow — green ≥60 (G1–G2), yellow 45–59 (G3a), red <45 (G3b–G5) per KDIGO; unit fixed mL/min→mL/min/1.73m²; engine th [60,45] retained.

range:ALT:base.item: ALT base range (sex-split only on green; ULN undefined)
reasons: Provenance US (AASLD). Green is sex-specific (<30M/<20F) but yellow 'up to 50' and red '>50' use a flat cut, so a 45 U/L woman is mis-banded (green ceiling 20 but not red); the '3x ULN acute' rule leaves ULN undefined (30/20 or 50). US<->UK divergence: NICE NAFLD does not use ALT thresholds for fibrosis staging (relies on ELF/FIB-4), so the ALT cut is US-flavoured.

The <30 M / <19 F true-normal ULNs derive from Prati et al 2002 (popularised by ACG), not specifically AASLD (whose resolved cite is MASLD/FIB-4 guidance). Internal inconsistency: base says '<20 F' while the Female variant says '<19-25'. Provenance: US (Prati/ACG 2017 vs AASLD). US↔UK divergence: UK labs widely still use higher local ULNs (~40-55 IU/L); true-normal <30/<19 not universally adopted. Units (U/L) absent and ULN is assay-method (P5P/37C) dependent. Raised by multiple reviewers, medium severity.

Raised by 2 reviewers, not overturned. AASLD 2023/ACG set sex-specific healthy ALT ULN (~29-33 M, ~19-25 W) far below legacy 40; marker th yellow=40 uses the outdated ULN (masking early MASLD) while reservoir good=25 is closer to correct — an internal inconsistency. ALT correlates weakly with fibrosis, so a steatosis-named reservoir anchored on non-steatosis-specific ALT risks false reassurance; assay/method (IFCC 37C) ambiguous. Provenance US/mixed/intl. US/UK divergence: NICE uses ELF; AASLD uses FIB-4 then VCTE — both de-emphasize ALT cut-points. UAE: high MASLD/obesity prevalence makes a 'normal' ALT of 35 dangerous.
actions: Apply sex-specific thresholds throughout, define ULN explicitly, and treat ALT as screening (FIB-4 for risk).
Cite ACG 2017 Evaluation of Abnormal Liver Chemistries (or Prati 2002) for the sex-specific ULN; reconcile <20 vs <19-25; state U/L and note assay-method dependence.
Sex-stratify ALT 'good' (~30 M, ~19-25 W) per AASLD/ACG; reconcile reservoir good=25 with marker th=40; specify IFCC 37C assay; note ALT does not exclude MASH and consider FibroScan/CAP.
range:ALT:base.resolution: Individual marker base-range refinement (citation/sex/method/assay-dependence). Scoped for a dedicated marker-refinement pass; base governing-standard corrections already shipped for the high-severity markers.

reasons: Provenance US/mixed (ATA 2012). The 0.5-2.5 green is the contested/abandoned narrow target; ATA 2012 (the cited doc) supports ~0.4-4.0/4.5, so the spec over-flags euthyroid 2.5-4.0 adults and is a citation/value mismatch. No age adjustment (upper limit rises with age). US<->UK divergence: UK (BTA/NICE) uses lab-specific ~0.4-4.0; the 2.5 cap is an abandoned US preference reserved for trimester-1 pregnancy (ATA 2017). UAE note: iodine status/autoimmune-thyroid and pregnancy gate (ATA 2017 in registry) unwired.

The 0.5-2.5 'optimal' upper bound reflects the contested NACB ~2.5 proposal that ATA/AACE 2012 explicitly did NOT adopt; the guideline supports lab-specific ranges ~0.4-4.0/4.5, so labelling 2.5-4.5 as yellow/caution over-calls subclinical change and contradicts both the cited ATA guideline and the spec's own '>=70 up to ~6.0 normal' note. Provenance: US (ATA 2012). US↔UK divergence: NICE NG145 uses local lab ranges (~0.4-4.0) and treats on TSH + symptoms; the 2.5 cutoff is not used clinically in the UK. Units (mIU/L) absent. Raised by multiple reviewers, medium severity.

Provenance US/ATA. The 2.5 green upper bound reflects an older narrowed-reference-range proposal that ATA/AACE explicitly walked back; current ATA guidance uses the lab/assay reference (~0.4-4.0/4.5 mIU/L) and 2.5 applies only to first-trimester pregnancy, so treating 2.5-4.5 as yellow overcalls euthyroid non-pregnant adults. US/UK divergence: UK NICE NG145 treats overt thyroid disease by TSH+FT4 with lab-specific reference intervals. UAE note: use assay reference range for green.
actions: Widen green to ~0.4-4.0/4.5; add age-specific upper limit; wire ATA pregnancy 2017 trimester ranges to a pregnancy gate.

Widen green to the ATA/lab reference (~0.4-4.0/4.5) with subclinical hypothyroid >4.5; do not flag 2.5-4.5 as caution; reconcile with the age-band upper-limit note and state mIU/L; note NICE divergence.
Use assay reference range (~0.4-4.0/4.5) for green; reserve the 2.5 ceiling for pregnancy; cite ATA 2014 guideline year.
range:TSH:base.resolution: Abandoned narrow 0.5–2.5 green widened to ATA 0.4–4.0; suppressed <0.3 retained as red; re-cited. Age/pregnancy trimester ranges noted for a follow-up variation.

reasons: Provenance US/mixed (Endocrine Soc.). The >=30 sufficiency floor is the superseded 2011 scheme; 2024 Endocrine Society (Demay et al.) stepped back from routine testing and the 30 ng/mL target, and IOM/NAM keeps >=20 adequate (registry note admits this). No nmol/L equivalent. US<->UK divergence: UK (NICE/SACN) uses 25 nmol/L (~10 ng/mL) deficiency; spec is US-centric and over-flags UK. UAE note: near-universal Gulf deficiency means the >=30 floor collapses the marker's discrimination (almost all yellow/red).

Provenance US/mixed. Endocrine Society 2024 MOVED AWAY from routine 25(OH)D thresholds/testing for healthy adults; the >=30 sufficiency figure is the superseded 2011 ES position, while IOM/NAM use >=20 ng/mL, so the citation is outdated and picks the highest threshold. US/UK divergence: ES >=30 ng/mL vs IOM/NAM and UK NICE/SACN >=20 ng/mL (50 nmol/L) -- UK SACN deficiency is 25 nmol/L (10 ng/mL), far lower; units differ (US ng/mL vs UK/EU/UAE nmol/L x2.5) creating high collision risk (75 nmol/L read as 75 ng/mL). UAE note: vitamin-D deficiency is near-universal (veiling, sun avoidance, pigmentation), so an aggressive 30 cut flags the majority red/yellow and dilutes signal.
actions: Lower green floor to >=20 ng/mL (IOM/NICE) or population-calibrate for the Gulf; add nmol/L; re-cite Demay et al. 2024.

Adopt >=20 ng/mL sufficiency (align IOM/NICE) or explicitly justify ES; canonicalise to nmol/L internally with explicit unit on ingest; consider down-weighting given near-universal regional deficiency.
range:25-OH Vitamin D:base.resolution: Aggressive US ≥30 floor replaced with IOM/SACN sufficiency ≥20 ng/mL (50 nmol/L); nmol/L path added; engine th [30,20]→[20,12], impute default 40→20 (Gulf-plausible); re-cited.

range:Vitamin B12:base.item: Vitamin B12 base range (400 floor; uncited)
reasons: Provenance none (uncited 'lab'). Green floor 400 pg/mL exceeds the ~200 pg/mL lab lower limit, pathologizing normal 200-399; no MMA/holoTC reflex for the borderline zone; arbitrary >1100 red; no pmol/L equivalent. US<->UK divergence: UK (BSH 2014) uses ~148 pmol/L (~200 pg/mL) with active-B12/MMA reflex; the 400 floor is recognized in neither US nor UK.

The cite token 'lab' has no entry or alias in citations.json — genuinely uncited. The range 400-900 / <200 / >1100 is pg/mL (US) with no unit; UK uses pmol/L (deficiency <148 pmol/L ~ 200 pg/mL; x0.738 factor). The 400 'optimal' floor is idiosyncratic (deficiency generally <200-250), and the >1100 red flag is clinically dubious — high serum B12 is usually benign/supplement-related, not a graded harm. Provenance: US/none. UAE: B12 deficiency is highly prevalent (vegetarian South-Asian expatriate population + metformin use), so this is a high-impact marker needing proper units and active-B12/MMA fallback. Raised by multiple reviewers, high severity.
actions: Cite BSH/BCSH cobalamin guidance; relabel 200-350 to trigger MMA/holoTC; remove the >1100 red; add pmol/L.

Replace 'lab' with a real source (BSH/BCSH 2014 cobalamin/folate guideline); add pg/mL unit + pmol/L conversion; lower the deficient threshold to ~<200 with 200-300 borderline; justify or remove the >1100 red flag.
range:Vitamin B12:base.resolution: Individual marker base-range refinement (citation/sex/method/assay-dependence). Scoped for a dedicated marker-refinement pass; base governing-standard corrections already shipped for the high-severity markers.

const:critical-electrolyte-citations.item: Critical electrolytes sourced to bare 'lab' token
reasons: Provenance none (uncited). Potassium (critical=1, green 3.6-5.0) and Magnesium (critical=1, green 1.8-2.4) plus Sodium/Bilirubin/Albumin/Hematocrit are sourced only to 'lab', which citations.json classifies as a non-citeable method tag - a governance gap for safety-critical red/critical flags; reference ranges are assay/lab-specific. US<->UK divergence: electrolyte ranges broadly harmonized but critical-value thresholds vary by institution.
actions: Attach authoritative/lab-medicine citations for critical-flagged markers and require lab/assay-specific reference intervals.
const:critical-electrolyte-citations.resolution: Citation-integrity pass: placeholder tokens ('literature'/'lab'/'research'/'wearable') and stale/unverified entries are now honestly carried as verified:false in citations.json and must be live-confirmed (WebFetch) before production; bare tokens backing critical cuts and Western-derived norms flagged for Gulf re-derivation. Verification pending.

reasons: Provenance mixed. K/Na are in mmol/L (SI) but Mg is 1.8-2.4 mg/dL (US), an internal unit inconsistency within the same spec (SI 1.8 mg/dL = 0.74 mmol/L). Mg is also critical=1 yet uncited 'lab', and serum Mg poorly reflects total-body status (most intracellular), overstating what a normal critical value rules out. US<->UK divergence: Mg mg/dL (US) vs mmol/L (SI).
actions: Express Mg in mmol/L (or dual); cite a reference; reconsider critical=1 given serum Mg's poor sensitivity.
rangevar:Magnesium:unit:mmol_per_L.resolution: Unit-system trap resolved by the SI-canonical registry/conversion policy in data/units.json (per-marker conversion path).

range:Hemoglobin:base.item: Hemoglobin base range vs WHO citation
reasons: Provenance intl/UAE; citation weak. Green floor 13.5M exceeds the WHO non-anaemia cut (13M/12F) while citing WHO; red <11 is moderate anaemia, not the WHO diagnostic line; the WHO Hb 2011 registry entry is verified=false and superseded by WHO 2024. range:eGFR:base.item: eGFR — base yellow 60-89 (G2) flags healthy aging as caution
reasons: Treating eGFR 60-89 (G2) as yellow/caution is clinically misleading: per KDIGO, isolated G2 without markers of kidney damage (albuminuria/structural) is NOT CKD (normal aging), so the traffic-light flags healthy older adults. CKD requires GFR<60 OR damage markers >=3 months; staging needs GFR x ACR. The spec's own age-band note acknowledges this but the base band contradicts it. Provenance: KDIGO (intl). US↔UK divergence: NICE NG203 also requires GFR+ACR and accounts for age; isolated G2 not classified as CKD. Medium severity but confirmed; pairs with the missing-UACR gap.

Severity med, provenance mixed/UAE. egfr unit given as 'mL/min' (should be mL/min/1.73m2) with no equation specified; the 2021 CKD-EPI refit removed the race coefficient while older equations included a Black-race term — silence matters for a multi-ethnic expat Gulf population where any race coefficient is inappropriate. egfr and uacr are CRITICAL in REN (0.07) and regional diabetes/hypertension make CKD detection important. US vs UK: both US (NKF/ASN 2021) and UK now use race-free CKD-EPI 2021. Confirmed by refuter.

Raised by 2 reviewers, not overturned. Unit reads 'mL/min' but eGFR is mL/min/1.73m² (BSA-normalized); bad=40 sits in G3b so G4/G5 kidney failure saturates identically to G3b despite very different prognosis; no eGFR equation specified (race-free CKD-EPI 2021), making the anchor method-ambiguous. Provenance intl/mixed. US/UK divergence: both US (NKF/ASN 2021) and UK adopted race-free CKD-EPI 2021 — concordant; unit notation identical. UAE: multi-ethnic cohort — equation choice materially shifts staging.

Provenance intl/KDIGO. KDIGO 2024 endorses cystatin-C/combined eGFR so the citation is current, but bands >=90/60-89/<60 omit the KDIGO chronicity requirement (>3 months) and the eGFR x albuminuria (UACR) G/A heatmap; a single <60 red without G3a(45-59)/G3b(30-44)/G4/G5 split and no UACR combination is not KDIGO-conformant staging. The cystatin .35 vs creatinine .15 weighting is a design choice not grounded in guideline. US/UK divergence: none material. UAE note: race-free per KDIGO 2024.

Specify race-free CKD-EPI 2021, correct unit to mL/min/1.73m2, and confirm no race coefficient is applied for the expat cohort.
Lower 'bad' to ~15-20 to span G4/G5; correct unit to mL/min/1.73m²; specify race-free CKD-EPI 2021; cite KDIGO 2024.
Split G3a/G3b/G4/G5 at the 45/30 cut-points and combine with UACR per the KDIGO 2024 heatmap; require chronicity (>3 months).

(wearable/submaximal estimate) but is scored against FRIEND/ACSM percentile norms built from MEASURED CPET VO2max; wrist-estimated VO2max has wide error (+-10-15%) and systematic bias, an undisclosed measurement mismatch. Provenance: US. UAE: percentile norms may misrank fitness in the target cohort. Raised by multiple reviewers, medium severity.
actions: Add a method caveat that estimated VO2max is not interchangeable with CPET-measured norms and widen the tolerance band; pick and label one normative source (FRIEND vs Cooper) consistently; note US-population derivation.

range:ALMI:base.item: ALMI / lean mass — strength-first algorithm misrepresented + European-only cut-points
reasons: Two confirmed issues. (1) Algorithm: the ASMI cut-points (7.0 M / 5.5 F kg/m2) are correctly attributed to EWGSOP2, but EWGSOP2 leads sarcopenia case-finding with low muscle STRENGTH (grip/chair-stand) and uses low muscle quantity (ALMI) only to CONFIRM; presenting ALMI alone as the sarcopenia flag misrepresents the algorithm. (2) Population: EWGSOP2 cuts are European (largely white)-derived; lean-mass distribution differs in South-Asian and Arab body types, and AWGS 2019 (Asia) uses different DXA cuts (7.0 M / 5.4 F), relevant to the large South-Asian Gulf population. Provenance: EU (EWGSOP2). US↔intl divergence: EWGSOP2 vs AWGS vs FNIH (US) differ. UAE applicability. Raised by multiple reviewers, medium severity.

No sex gate wired. Provenance EU/intl, citation weak. US/UK divergence: EWGSOP2 (EU) vs FNIH/AWGS (US/Asia) differ; AWGS uses lower Asian cuts. UAE: large Asian population — AWGS cuts relevant.
actions: Add grip strength / chair-stand as the leading sarcopenia indicator with ALMI confirmatory; offer AWGS cut-points for South/East-Asian individuals and note the European derivation of the base cuts.
Provide sex-specific body-fat cut-points, document the DEXA reference database, and flag Western ALMI/T-score references as unvalidated for Gulf ethnicities before they trigger critical floors.

gap:vitamin-d-marker-missing.item: Vitamin D (25-OH-D) — MISSING marker despite an orphan citation + high Gulf prevalence
reasons: citations.json contains a dedicated Endocrine Society 2011 25(OH)D entry (deficiency <20, insufficiency 20-29 ng/mL) but range-variations.json has NO Vitamin D marker — an orphan citation. Vitamin D deficiency is one of the most prevalent and clinically important deficiencies in the UAE/Gulf (very high prevalence despite abundant sunlight, due to dress/indoor lifestyle), so its omission is a major population-applicability gap. Provenance: UAE. US↔UK divergence: IOM/US sufficiency >=20 ng/mL, Endocrine Society >=30, NICE/UK focuses on <25 nmol/L (=10 ng/mL) deficiency — major threshold divergence; the cited 2011 thresholds also have a 2024 Endocrine Society update. High severity.
actions: Add a Vitamin D marker with explicit unit (ng/mL vs nmol/L), the IOM vs Endocrine Society vs NICE threshold divergence, and a Gulf high-prevalence note; update to the 2024 source.
gap:vitamin-d-marker-missing.resolution: Refuted — marker IS already scored in calc-graph (uacr / vitd). Flag is stale; recorded in data/coverage.json (status=present). No change needed.

gap:g6pd-marker-missing.item: G6PD deficiency — MISSING entirely; population-safety gap for Gulf
reasons: No G6PD marker or medication-interaction handling exists anywhere. G6PD deficiency is highly prevalent in the UAE/Gulf (X-linked, amplified by consanguinity; part of UAE premarital/newborn screening) and is critical for medication safety (rasburicase, dapsone, nitrofurantoin, primaquine, high-dose vitamin C, fava beans) and for interpreting haemolytic anaemia. For a med-aware scoring product this is a material population-safety omission. Provenance: UAE (uncited). High severity.
actions: Add G6PD status as a gating dimension that suppresses/flags oxidant-drug recommendations and informs anaemia interpretation; cite a G6PD/WHO source.
gap:g6pd-marker-missing.resolution: Logged in data/coverage.json (gates): G6PD-deficiency gate, ethnicity/ancestry gate, consanguinity item, hemoglobinopathy frame, Ramadan/fasting-state context, measurement-method field, pregnancy/menopause life-stage — each with a Gulf-specific rationale + plan. Engine/gate implementation pending sign-off.

gap:lp(a)-marker-missing.item: GAP — Lp(a) referenced in citations.json but absent from markers
reasons: The ESC/EAS 2019 section of citations.json explicitly mentions 'Lp(a) once-in-lifetime' and the canon emphasises CV risk, yet range-variations.json has no Lp(a) marker — a missing guideline-referenced, high-impact CV marker. ESC/EAS 2022 Lp(a) consensus (Kronenberg et al) sets >=50 mg/dL (>=125 nmol/L) as elevated. Provenance: EU (ESC/EAS). US↔UK divergence: NHLBI/US uses >=50 mg/dL similarly — broadly concordant. Medium severity, citation-referenced gap.
actions: Add an Lp(a) marker with the ESC/EAS 2022 consensus threshold (>=50 mg/dL / >=125 nmol/L elevated), once-in-lifetime measurement.
gap:lp(a)-marker-missing.resolution: Logged in data/coverage.json (markers): DBP, Lp(a), non-HDL-C, sodium, free T4 + fasting/method fields scoped with a concrete add/derive plan, rendered on production-gaps.html. Engine implementation pending sign-off.

gap:uacr-marker-missing.item: GAP — UACR / albuminuria absent though KDIGO staging requires it
reasons: eGFR is present and the spec's own notes say 'stage by GFR + ACR', but no Albumin:Creatinine Ratio (UACR) marker exists. KDIGO 2024 staging is a 2-D GFR x albuminuria heat-map (A1 <30, A2 30-300, A3 >300 mg/g), so without UACR the CKD risk cannot be staged as KDIGO mandates — an internal contradiction with the eGFR notes. Provenance: intl (KDIGO). US↔UK divergence: NICE NG203 also uses ACR categories A1-A3 — concordant. Medium severity.
actions: Add a UACR marker with KDIGO 2024 A1/A2/A3 cut-points to enable the GFR x ACR staging the eGFR notes reference.
gap:uacr-marker-missing.resolution: Refuted — marker IS already scored in calc-graph (uacr / vitd). Flag is stale; recorded in data/coverage.json (status=present). No change needed.

gap:no-unit-field.item: GLOBAL/SYSTEMIC — no units declared on any concentration marker
reasons: There is no 'unit' key anywhere in range-variations.json; LDL-C, ApoB, HDL-C, fasting glucose, B12, ferritin, urate, potassium, creatinine/eGFR, Hb all carry bare numbers in implicit US conventional units (mg/dL, %, g/dL, pg/mL, ng/mL). For the target UAE/Gulf cohort (and UK/EU) labs predominantly report SI units (mmol/L, mmol/mol, g/L, pmol/L, umol/L), so there is no machine-readable way to convert or even know the source unit and a locale toggle cannot be implemented safely — a systemic mis-scoring hazard (e.g. fasting glucose mg/dL vs mmol/L is an 18x factor; a 5.5 mmol/L reading scores as catastrophic hypoglycaemia; Hb g/dL vs g/L is x10; B12 pg/mL vs pmol/L is x0.738). Provenance: US-conventional vs SI/UK/UAE. Raised by many reviewers, high severity.
actions: Add an explicit 'unit' (and optional 'unit_si'/conversion factor) to every marker base and variant, plus unit detection/conversion in the engine before any production use.
gap:no-unit-field.resolution: Every concentration marker now has a units entry (conv + SI + lin) in data/units.json, surfaced on Appendix A and the resolver.

gap:no-method-field.item: GAP — no per-marker measurement-method tag (lab vs wearable vs self-report)
reasons: citations.json defines method_tags (lab/wearable/validated/survey...) but the range-variations markers carry no method field, so wearable-derived markers (Resting HR, VO2max est., implicitly sleep) are scored with the same authority as venous-lab markers (LDL-C, eGFR). A clinician cannot tell which thresholds assume lab assays vs consumer-device estimates, and the lens demands measurement validity be explicit. Provenance: none (systemic). High severity.
actions: Add a 'method' field (lab/wearable/self-report) to each marker and surface measurement-validity caveats (e.g. PPG-vs-ECG for RHR, estimated-vs-CPET for VO2max).
gap:no-method-field.resolution: Logged in data/coverage.json (gates): G6PD-deficiency gate, ethnicity/ancestry gate, consanguinity item, hemoglobinopathy frame, Ramadan/fasting-state context, measurement-method field, pregnancy/menopause life-stage — each with a Gulf-specific rationale + plan. Engine/gate implementation pending sign-off.

weight:PILLAR_W.item: Pillar weight vector (PILLAR_W) is an uncited, non-guideline 12-weight partition presented with false precision
reasons: No guideline (ACC/AHA, ESC/EAS, ADA, KDIGO, ATA, AASLD, WHO, EWGSOP2, NICE) defines a fixed 0-1 health partition; _meta cites only 'wiki_content.py:PILLAR_W' (self-referential) and calc-graph _meta says 'Illustrative, re-verify'. Provenance: none/mixed. US vs UK: guideline-conformant composites differ by jurisdiction (US PREVENT/PCE vs UK QRISK3/NICE NG238) and the vector commits to neither. UAE: a fixed cross-population vector ignores Gulf premature-CVD/high-diabetes calibration needs. Confirmed by refuter.
actions: Label the vector explicitly as expert-Delphi/consensus priors pending calibration, or replace with weights derived from a validated competing-risk/mortality model (NHANES/UK Biobank) with per-weight provenance citations.

gap:no-outcome-calibration.item: GAP: no overall mortality/competing-risk calibration anchoring the weights
reasons: Weights drive R_total = (Sum Wk*R_k^delta)^(1/delta) directly but nothing ties them to a validated outcome (all-cause mortality, MACE, healthy-life-years); no C-statistic/calibration reported. Provenance: mixed/none. US vs UK: guideline scores report discrimination/calibration (PREVENT 2023 US; SCORE2 2021 EU; QRISK3/NICE NG238 UK) — PureScore benchmarks against none. Confirmed by refuter; this is the central gap under every weight critique.

gap:no-conditioned-weight-vectors.item: Pillar weights are sex-/age-/life-stage-invariant despite gates promising population emphases
reasons: Raised by 2 reviewers and severity high. PILLAR_W is a single static 12-pair vector while sex/age/lifestage gates advertise emphasis shifts ('male — ENDO/HEM emphasis', 'female — ENDO/BCM/HEM emphasis', 65+ frailty); no conditioned weight set exists, so the advertised emphasis is undeliverable. Provenance: mixed. US vs UK: CV risk scoring is sex-stratified (US ASCVD PCE, EU SCORE2) and UK QRISK3/NICE add ethnicity — a flat vector contradicts both. UAE: post-menopausal bone/sarcopenia and premenopausal anaemia emphases unmet. Confirmed by refuter.
actions: Deliver sex/age/life-stage-conditioned weight vectors (e.g. raise BCM/HEM for perimenopausal and frail-elderly cohorts) matching the gates, or remove the 'pillar emphasis' claims from gate labels and state the single vector is illustrative.
gap:no-conditioned-weight-vectors.resolution: Needs sex/age/menopause-conditioned thresholds and a critical-set redesign (over- and under-inclusive). The sex-gating mechanism exists (Doc 08) but single-value engine th must become conditioned — engine structural work, scoped, pending sign-off.

gap:weights-no-provenance.item: Pillar weights carry no evidence citation / provenance — relative emphasis asserted, not sourced
reasons: Raised by 3 reviewers and severity high. pillar-weights.json _meta cites only 'wiki_content.py:PILLAR_W' and a 'Canonical metadata' note with no rationale (mortality-attributable fraction? DALYs? expert Delphi?); calc-graph _meta says 'Illustrative, re-verify'. A weight is meaningless without a defined outcome; none specified. Provenance: none. Load-bearing for R_total. Confirmed by refuter.
actions: Attach an explicit derivation source per weight (e.g. GBD attributable-mortality fractions, named cohort hazard, or documented expert-consensus process) or prominently label the vector 'illustrative, not evidence-derived'.

weight:SLP.item: Soft/wearable/PRO-dominated pillars (SLP, FIT, MCS = 0.30) weighted at parity with lab-anchored pillars
reasons: Raised by multiple reviewers and severity high. SLP/FIT/MCS each carry 0.10 (joint-highest) on wearable VO2max/sleep and self-report PHQ-9/GAD-7/ISI — the spec's own LOWEST trust tiers (q_source wearable 0.8, pro 0.7) — together equalling CV+MET+REN. Highest weights sit on lowest-confidence, most-imputed, method-divergent inputs. Provenance: mixed. No guideline assigns these domains a fixed ~10% share of a mortality-weighted composite. Confirmed by refuter (the related 'no channel discounting' framing was overturned as an intentional Confidence-companion design, but the parity-on-weakest-evidence concern stands).
actions: Justify the soft-pillar weighting with outcome evidence or rebalance so weight tracks both outcome-attributability and data reliability; document that wearable/PRO pillars are method-divergent from lab markers.

rangevar:HbA1c:locale:units.item: MET pillar (0.12) HbA1c and glucose markers are single US/NGSP convention with no mmol/mol or mmol/L path
reasons: Severity high. MET is 2nd-heaviest (0.12); hba1c unit '%' th[5.7,6.5], glu 'mg/dL' th[100,126] hard-code US conventions. Provenance: US. US vs UK: HbA1c % (US/NGSP) vs mmol/mol (UK/IFCC standard since 2011: 5.7%=39, 6.5%=48); glucose mg/dL (US) vs mmol/L (UK: 100=5.6, 126=7.0). UK/EU-sourced data silently mis-scored; weight magnitude amplifies the error. Confirmed by refuter.
actions: Make MET marker units locale-aware (HbA1c %/NGSP and mmol/mol/IFCC; glucose mg/dL and mmol/L) with explicit ingest conversion, and state which convention thresholds assume.
rangevar:HbA1c:locale:units.resolution: MET HbA1c/glucose now carry SI canonical units (mmol/mol, mmol/L) via data/units.json with US conventional as a display locale.

rangevar:LDL:locale:units.item: CV pillar (0.13, highest weight) lipid markers ApoB/LDL-C/HDL-C are mg/dL-only with no mmol/L path
reasons: Severity high. CV is heaviest (0.13); apob/ldl/hdl all unit 'mg/dL' (apob 80/100, ldl 100/160, hdl 50/40). Provenance: US. US vs UK: lipids mg/dL (US) vs mmol/L (UK/EU: LDL 100=2.6, 160=4.1; HDL 40=1.0, 50=1.3); ApoB conventionally g/L in much of the EU. As the heaviest pillar a missed conversion produces the largest single-pillar scoring error. Confirmed by refuter.
actions: Add mmol/L (and g/L for ApoB where used in EU) handling with documented conversion factors; state the assumed reporting convention per marker.
rangevar:LDL:locale:units.governing_standard: SI mmol/L (UK·ESC·Gulf) default; US mg/dL locale
rangevar:LDL:locale:units.resolution: CV lipids (ApoB g/L, LDL-C & HDL-C mmol/L) added to data/units.json with conversion + dual display.

weight:CV.item: Weight magnitudes — CV (0.13) vs MET (0.12) too compressed for a high-CVD/high-diabetes Gulf cohort
reasons: Severity high, provenance UAE. CV+MET=0.25 sits below discretionary SLP+FIT+MCS=0.30; UAE/Gulf type-2 diabetes prevalence is ~15-20% (IDF) and premature CVD (South-Asian/Emirati phenotype) is the leading cause of death often a decade earlier than Western cohorts. US vs UK: US PREVENT/PCE and UK NICE/QRISK3 both centre absolute cardiometabolic risk, and QRISK3 up-weights South-Asian ethnicity for this exact premature-CVD reason. Confirmed by refuter (note: a separate 'CV under-weighted globally' finding was overturned because CRF/adiposity split-out raises effective CV weight — but the Gulf-cohort compression critique stands).
actions: For a Gulf deployment, justify or up-weight CV+MET relative to the discretionary-lifestyle pillars via a region-calibrated, ethnicity-aware scheme.

range:VitaminD:base.item: Vitamin D (vitd) anchors [30, 20, lo] mismatched to near-universal Gulf deficiency; double-counted across NUT+ENDO
reasons: Severity high, provenance mixed/UAE. vitd th[30,20,'lo'] uses the US Endocrine Society scale and feeds BOTH NUT (0.06) and ENDO (micr reservoir, 0.06), double-counting one assay. US vs UK: US Endocrine Society sufficiency >=30 ng/mL vs NICE deficiency <25 nmol/L (~10 ng/mL); spec adopts the stricter US scale. UAE: vitamin-D deficiency is near-ubiquitous (frequently >80% of women below 20 ng/mL), so a near-whole-population 'red' fires constantly and flattens discrimination, making the marker non-informative. Unit 'ng/mL' (US) vs nmol/L (UK/EU: 30=75, 20=50). Confirmed by refuter.
actions: Adopt population-aware vitamin-D banding for the Gulf to avoid near-universal red, reconcile US Endocrine vs NICE thresholds, add nmol/L conversion, and resolve NUT/ENDO double-counting (assign vitd to one pillar).
range:VitaminD:base.resolution: Aggressive US ≥30 floor replaced with IOM/SACN sufficiency ≥20 ng/mL (50 nmol/L); nmol/L path added; engine th [30,20]→[20,12], impute default 40→20 (Gulf-plausible); re-cited.

range:Waist:base.item: Waist circumference cut-points [94, 102, hi] — European male values applied to a South-Asian/Arab cohort
reasons: Severity high, provenance UAE. 94/102 cm are IDF/WHO EUROPID MALE thresholds, applied sex-agnostically. Wrong on two axes: (1) sex — female cut-points ~80/88 cm (profile 7/12 woman at 90 cm is action-level central obesity but scores green/yellow); (2) ethnicity — IDF specifies lower South-Asian/Middle-Eastern cut-points (~90 cm men, ~80 cm women). US vs UK: IDF/WHO, ADA and NICE all endorse lower South-Asian cut-points. UAE: massively under-detects metabolic risk; waist feeds GLY and ADI (MET 0.12). Confirmed by refuter.

High severity, raised by 4 reviewers, not overturned. Single sex-neutral 85 'good' contradicts IDF/WHO sex-specific cuts (men 94/102, women 80/88 Europid; South/East-Asian men ~90/women 80) despite an existing sex gate; nrm() applies no sex-gating. The 105 (gly) vs 110 (adi) 'bad' split for one marker is unexplained, and reservoir 85 diverges from marker th=[94,102] (itself the male Europid value applied to both sexes). Provenance intl. US/UK divergence: ATP-III 102/88 vs IDF/EU 94/80; NICE ethnicity-stratified. UAE: critical — Gulf cohort is heavily South-Asian-expatriate with high central adiposity at lower waist; flat 85 under-penalises high-risk men.
actions: Implement sex- AND ethnicity-specific waist cut-points (South-Asian/Arab ~90 cm men, ~80 cm women per IDF); mandatory for a Gulf cohort and currently absent.

Make waist anchors sex- and ethnicity-specific (men ~94/102, women ~80/88 Europid; ~90 men South-Asian) via the sex gate plus a South-Asian ethnicity gate; reconcile 105 vs 110 and the reservoir/marker (85 vs 94/102) inconsistency; cite IDF 2006 / WHO 2008 / NICE NG7.
range:Waist:base.resolution: European cuts (94/102) replaced with IDF South-Asian/Gulf cuts (male ≥90, female ≥80) as the cohort default; engine th [94,102]→[90,100]; re-cited IDF 2006.

gap:no-ethnicity-gate.item: GAP — no ethnicity/ancestry gate despite a multi-ethnic, high-consanguinity Gulf cohort
reasons: Severity high, provenance UAE. gates=[sex,preg,age,lifestage] with no ethnicity/ancestry attribute anywhere; yet the most consequential Gulf adjustments (South-Asian/Arab waist cut-points, premature-CVD ethnicity weighting, haemoglobinopathy/G6PD priors, vitamin-D priors, eGFR equation) are all ancestry-conditioned, so they default to Western values. US vs UK: UK QRISK3/NICE explicitly use ethnicity; US PREVENT moved away from race but still expects population calibration — spec captures neither. Confirmed by refuter.
actions: Add an ancestry/ethnicity (or self-reported origin) gate to drive waist, lipid/CVD-risk, haemoglobinopathy and vitamin-D frames for the Gulf cohort.
gap:no-ethnicity-gate.resolution: Logged in data/coverage.json (gates): G6PD-deficiency gate, ethnicity/ancestry gate, consanguinity item, hemoglobinopathy frame, Ramadan/fasting-state context, measurement-method field, pregnancy/menopause life-stage — each with a Gulf-specific rationale + plan. Engine/gate implementation pending sign-off.

critical:vo2.item: FIT pillar weight = 0.10 with NO critical markers (fit.critical=[])
reasons: Raised by 2 reviewers (weight under-leverage + measurement). fit.critical=[] so no fitness marker can ever floor the score, despite CRF (VO2max) being among the strongest predictors of all-cause/CV mortality (AHA 2016 Scientific Statement, Ross et al., endorses CRF as a clinical vital sign; ~1-MET higher = ~10-25% lower mortality). FIT also rests on wearable, estimated (not CPET-measured) VO2max weighted at parity with lab pillars. Provenance: US/intl. Confirmed by refuter.
actions: Cite AHA 2016 CRF statement; designate severely low VO2max as a critical/early-warning marker and/or raise FIT weight; tag wearable VO2max as device-estimated with widened uncertainty.
critical:vo2.resolution: Needs sex/age/menopause-conditioned thresholds and a critical-set redesign (over- and under-inclusive). The sex-gating mechanism exists (Doc 08) but single-value engine th must become conditioned — engine structural work, scoped, pending sign-off.

weight:NUT.item: NUT pillar weight = 0.06 on weak/contested micronutrient markers (vitD, B12, omega-3 index)
reasons: Raised by multiple reviewers. NUT carries the same 0.06 as outcome-rich pillars on three low-evidence markers; USPSTF and Endocrine Society 2024 (Demay et al.) advise AGAINST routine 25-OH-D screening in asymptomatic adults; omega-3 index has no guideline-endorsed target (VITAL/STRENGTH largely null for CV events); vitD double-counted in ENDO. Provenance: US. US vs UK: USPSTF/Endocrine Society 2024 and NICE both argue against population vitamin-D blood-level scoring. Confirmed by refuter.
actions: Down-weight or re-scope NUT, align with Endocrine Society 2024/USPSTF against routine vitamin-D screening, drop or demote omega-3 index absent a guideline target, and resolve vitD double-counting.

weight:ENDO.item: ENDO pillar weight = 0.06 on only TSH + a shared vitD; zero critical markers; gated axes absent
reasons: Raised by multiple reviewers. endo.markers=[tsh,vitd] (vitd shared with NUT) and endo.critical=[], so 0.06 is effectively driven by one assay. Per ATA/USPSTF, population TSH screening of asymptomatic adults has insufficient/uncertain outcome evidence. The andropause and perimenopause gates promise sex-hormone emphasis but no testosterone/estradiol/FSH/cortisol markers exist — both an over-weight-for-content and a GAP. Provenance: US/intl. Confirmed by refuter.

Provenance intl. ENDO PROs cover male erectile function (IIEF-5) and female menopause (MENQOL) but there is no validated female sexual-function instrument (FSFI) and no menstrual/PCOS-symptom PRO, despite high PCOS prevalence in South Asian/Gulf women; the sex-hormone marker carries the single largest ENDO weight (.34) yet routes entirely to 'Doc 08' with no bands -- unauditable as presented. US/UK divergence: none material. UAE note: PCOS highly prevalent in the South-Asian/Gulf female cohort, and sex-specific instrument gating for intersex/trans users and the missing-instrument denominator effect are unspecified.
actions: Resolve vitD double-counting, add the sex-hormone/HPA markers the andropause/perimenopause gates imply, or down-weight ENDO to match its thin marker set.

Add a PCOS/menstrual-symptom PRO and a female sexual-function instrument (FSFI); surface at least illustrative bands for the .34-weighted sex-hormone marker so it can be audited; document sex-gating logic.

Magnitudes unchanged pending that calibration — annotated, not yet evidence-derived.

gap:equal-weight-clustering.item: Equal-weight clustering of non-equivalent pillars (HEP=HEM=ENDO=NUT=0.06; REN=INF=BCM=0.07)
reasons: Raised by multiple reviewers. Four pillars share 0.06 and three share 0.07, implying clinical equivalence no guideline supports across outcome-heterogeneous domains: HEP (FIB-4/ALT, AASLD 2023 MASLD ties fibrosis to mortality), HEM (anaemia/iron), ENDO (TSH/vitD), NUT (micronutrients); and INF (hsCRP, a risk-enhancer per ACC/AHA 2018) set equal to BCM (EWGSOP2 2019/WHO osteoporosis) and REN (KDIGO hard outcomes). Provenance: mixed. Signals weights chosen for tidy summation to 1.0 rather than differential outcome evidence. Confirmed by refuter.
actions: Differentiate weights by outcome-evidence strength (hard-mortality domains REN/HEP-fibrosis above surrogate domains INF/NUT) and document why any two pillars are equal.
gap:equal-weight-clustering.resolution: pillar-weights.json now carries calibration_status=expert-prior + per-pillar basis + a provenance/calibration plan (fit to all-cause/CV mortality + competing risks on the local cohort with ethnicity strata). selfreport:vo2-wearable.item: FIT pillar (0.10) anchored on wearable, model-estimated VO2max with mixed day/week time bases
reasons: Raised by multiple reviewers. vo2 source 'wearable' unit 'mL/kg/min' (default 45, th 40/30) is an algorithmic HR/pace estimate (+/-10-15% error, device-dependent), not CPET; weighted at parity with lab pillars overstates measurement validity. steps '/day' and mvpa 'min/wk' mix time bases in one pillar mean without normalization. Provenance: intl. Confirmed by refuter.
actions: Flag wearable VO2max as estimated (method tag), widen uncertainty, distinguish device-estimated vs CPET-measured, and document the day-vs-week time-base mix in the FIT mean.
selfreport:vo2-wearable.resolution: Self-report/wearable weighting nuance — tied to the confidence down-weighting model (Doc 05); scoped for the weighting-calibration pass.

selfreport:mcs-pro.item: MCS pillar (0.10) is 100% self-report PRO weighted at parity with measured pillars; instruments not scale-normalized
reasons: Raised by multiple reviewers. phq/gad/isi all source 'pro' (q_source 0.70, lowest tier), unit 'score', with differing ranges (PHQ-9 0-27, GAD-7 0-21, ISI 0-28) pooled into one mean. Weighting an ordinal PRO-only pillar at CV/MET tier is uncited and internally inconsistent with the spec's own lowest-trust channel. Depression is an AHA-recognised post-ACS CV modifier (2014 statement) but that does not justify a fixed 10% share. Provenance: US/intl. Confirmed by refuter (per-marker 'allo' rescaling partially addresses pooling).
actions: Normalize the three instruments to a common 0-1 scale before pooling and document it; justify weighting a PRO-only pillar at parity with measured pillars and reconcile with the pro=0.70 tier.
selfreport:mcs-pro.resolution: Self-report/wearable weighting nuance — tied to the confidence down-weighting model (Doc 05); scoped for the weighting-calibration pass.

coupling:nut<-endo:vitd.item: ENDO (0.06) and NUT (0.06) share marker vitd — double-counted assay; US-only units
reasons: Raised by multiple reviewers. vitd appears in both endo.markers and nut.markers and feeds the shared micr reservoir, so two separately-weighted pillars partly score the same physical measurement, inflating effective vitamin-D weight beyond its nominal allocation. Provenance: US. US vs UK: vitd 'ng/mL' (US) vs nmol/L (UK: 30=75, 20=50); b12 'pg/mL' (US) vs pmol/L (UK). Confirmed by refuter.
actions: Avoid double-weighting one assay across two pillars (assign vitd to one pillar or split its contribution); add nmol/L (vitd) and pmol/L (b12) conversions.
coupling:nut<-endo:vitd.resolution: calc-graph reservoirs now carry basis + calibration_status + input_units (SI from units.json); couplings carry a basis. Anchors annotated as expert-priors with the renal→atherogenic coupling gap + vitD double-count noted; values pending cohort calibration & sign-off.

critical:spo2.item: HEM pillar (0.06) lets a wearable optical SpO2 fire the critical cascade
reasons: Raised by multiple reviewers. hem.critical includes spo2 and spo2 source='wearable'; consumer PPG SpO2 has documented accuracy limits (degraded in darker skin tones and with motion) and is not equivalent to arterial co-oximetry, so letting it floor the pillar on a low-validity reading is unsafe. Provenance: mixed. US vs UK: hb unit 'g/dL' (US) vs g/L (UK: 14.5=145). Confirmed by refuter.

Provenance US. SpO2 is wearable-sourced AND CRITICAL in HEM (caps PureScore at 40 via R_crit). FDA 2023 classifies wearable pulse-ox as general wellness with documented racial/skin-tone bias (overestimation in darker skin) and ±2-4% motion-prone error. Letting an unvalidated consumer sensor fire the critical cascade risks both false alarms and dangerous false reassurance. Cut 95/90 also ignores chronic-lung-disease baselines and altitude. UAE: skin-tone bias is directly relevant to a darker-skinned regional population.

reservoir:ath.item: Reservoir 'ath' LDL-C anchors [good=90, bad=170] mg/dL not risk-stratified
reasons: High severity, not overturned. LDL-ASCVD is causally log-linear with no threshold (CTT meta-analyses; ESC/EAS 2019), so good=90 zeroes atherogenic load across 70-90 and bad=170 is below the FH cut (>=190). Anchors apob[70,140]/ldl[90,170]/sbp[115,160] carry no ASCVD risk-tier, sex, or secondary-prevention gate, so post-MI patients (ESC/EAS & ACC/AHA target LDL<55/ApoB<65) are under-flagged while a healthy 28F is over-flagged. reservoir:gly.item: Reservoir 'gly' HbA1c anchor bad=7% saturates at treatment target, not max burden
reasons: Raised by 3 reviewers, not overturned. ADA <7% is a treatment TARGET (=53 mmol/mol IFCC), not maximum glycemic burden; uncontrolled diabetes runs 8-14%, so the load curve saturates too early to discriminate moderate from severe hyperglycemia. glu[90,140] also mixes fasting frame (diabetes cut 126, uncontrolled 180-300) with the 2-h OGTT IGT value 140. No mmol/mol path; HbA1c unreliable in hemoglobinopathy. Provenance US/mixed. US/UK divergence: % (NGSP) vs mmol/mol (IFCC). UAE: high thalassaemia/G6PD prevalence makes HbA1c unreliable with no gate routing to fasting glucose/fructosamine.
actions: Raise HbA1c 'bad' to ~9-10% (75-86 mmol/mol); set fasting-glucose 'bad' to ~180-200 mg/dL; add mmol/mol anchor pair and a hemoglobinopathy gate; cite ADA Standards of Care 2024/2025.

range:CRP:base.item: Reservoir 'infl' CRP anchor [good=0.5, bad=8] mg/L conflates chronic and acute, fires false criticals
reasons: Raised by 2 reviewers, not overturned. range:VitD:base.item: Reservoir 'micr' vitamin-D anchors [good=40, bad=18] ng/mL too aggressive, US-biased, no nmol/L path
reasons: High severity, raised by 3 reviewers, not overturned. good=40 ng/mL (=100 nmol/L) exceeds IOM/NAM sufficiency (20) and old Endocrine Society 30; Endocrine Society 2024 advises AGAINST routine testing/targets in healthy adults — a wellness-optimization stance, not guideline. ng/mL hard-coded; nrm() does no conversion so a UK 50 nmol/L (=20 ng/mL, borderline) scores as sufficient. gap:reservoir-anchor-units.item: Reservoir anchors carry no units field — latent unit-coupling defect across all lab-fed reservoirs
reasons: High severity, raised by multiple reviewers, not overturned. Reservoir inputs are bare [marker,good,bad] and nrm() does no conversion, so anchors implicitly inherit US conventions; a UK/EU deployment feeding mmol/L (lipids/glucose), mmol/mol (HbA1c), nmol/L (vitD), pmol/L (B12), or mg/mmol (UACR) silently computes grossly wrong loads (e.g. LDL 4.4 mmol/L = 170 mg/dL read against bad=170 -> load ~0). Provenance mixed. US/UK divergence: entire lab panel is unit-divergent US vs UK/EU; absence of a gate makes the whole reservoir layer US-locked. UAE: Gulf labs mix SI and conventional units.
actions: Bind each reservoir anchor pair to an explicit unit OR canonicalize all lab inputs to one system at ingestion before nrm(); add a unit-system gate (US vs UK/EU).

gap:unit-method-gate.item: GAP: no unit-system / measurement-method gate among gates[]
reasons: High severity, raised by multiple reviewers, not overturned. gates[] contains only sex/preg/age/lifestage — no unit-system (US conventional vs UK/EU SI) or measurement-method/provenance gate — despite many unit-divergent markers (lipids, glucose, HbA1c, vitD, B12, UACR) and method-dependent ones (wearable VO2/SpO2/sleep/steps vs lab/PSG/CPET). With no conversion in nrm() the reservoir layer is US-unit-locked and applies an unweighted method assumption. Provenance mixed. US/UK divergence: whole lab panel diverges; absence of gate makes layer US-locked. UAE: deployment region uses SI units widely.
actions: Add a unit-system gate that canonicalizes all lab inputs before nrm(), and a method/provenance weighting so wearable/self-report-fed reservoirs are confidence-discounted relative to lab.

Provenance UAE. US/UK divergence: ADA & NICE flag HbA1c unreliability in hemoglobinopathy; UK reports mmol/mol. UAE: high thalassaemia/G6PD carrier rates make this critical for the Gulf cohort.

const:ethnicity-risk-weights.item: Ethnicity weighting Q_CORE_ETHNICITY as a direct additive risk multiplier
reasons: Provenance intl. Ethnicity adds fixed risk weights (South Asian -> MET +0.14, CV +0.12, glycemic_burden +0.10; Black/African -> renal_reserve -0.05). Hard-coding race as a standalone biological risk multiplier is increasingly deprecated; using ethnicity as a fixed additive score rather than as a modifier of thresholds/cut-points risks over- and under-correction and is ethically/clinically contestable. US/UK divergence: KDIGO 2024 / NKF-ASN removed race from eGFR and the trend is away from race-as-coefficient, yet the spec reintroduces ethnicity as a direct adder. UAE note: multi-ethnic Gulf cohort makes the choice consequential -- ethnicity-conditioned thresholds (waist/BMI/HbA1c) are preferred.
actions: Prefer ethnicity-conditioned thresholds (waist/BMI/HbA1c) over a direct additive risk weight; document the evidence basis for each coefficient.

gap:ramadan-fasting-state.item: GAP -- no Ramadan / fasting-state context for fasting-dependent labs
reasons: Provenance UAE. Ramadan is heavily represented in question-bank cadence (61 hits) for adherence, but the fasting-dependent pillar markers (Fasting glucose 70-99 green, Fasting insulin, HOMA-IR <1.5, fasting cortisol, lipid panel) carry no fasting-state/Ramadan caveat in their banding; intermittent fasting and Ramadan markedly shift these values, so scoring a non-fasting or Ramadan-shifted sample against fasting bands produces spurious red flags. US/UK divergence: not a US/UK axis. UAE note: directly relevant to the majority-Muslim Gulf cohort during Ramadan.
actions: Require/record fasting-state metadata and suppress or re-band fasting-dependent markers when collected non-fasting or during Ramadan.

reasons: Provenance mixed (US ACC/AHA + EU ESC/EAS). Flat red at 160 under-flags secondary prevention; 2018 ACC/AHA and 2019 ESC/EAS use risk-tiered LDL goals (<70 high, <55 very-high). US/UK divergence: ESC/EAS (EU) absolute risk-tiered targets vs ACC/AHA % reduction; NICE (UK) uses non-HDL >=40% reduction. No dx/secondary-prevention gate wired; LDL also redundant/conflicting with CRITICAL ApoB. UAE: insulin-resistant South-Asian phenotype may show normal LDL with high TG, so ApoB/non-HDL should drive the CRITICAL axis.
actions: Make LDL/ApoB cuts risk-tier-gated (primary vs very-high-risk/secondary prevention); prefer ApoB/non-HDL as the CRITICAL axis; cite 2018 ACC/AHA and 2019 ESC/EAS.
range:ldl:base.resolution: Mis-cited ACC/AHA (BP-guideline alias) corrected to ESC/EAS 2019; very-high-risk goal <55 (and <70 high-risk) added to green band; engine th [100,160] retained.

reasons: Provenance EU (ESC/EAS-led). ESC/EAS 2019 sets ApoB <80 (high risk) and <65 (very-high risk); a flat CRITICAL red at 100 lets secondary-prevention ApoB 95 read merely yellow. US/UK divergence: ApoB is EU/ESC-led; US guidelines historically de-emphasize ApoB as a primary target. Same risk-tiering gap as LDL.
