range:apob:base.resolution: ApoB risk-tiered to ESC/EAS 2019 goals (<65 very-high, <80 high, <100 moderate); green <90; engine th [80,100]→[100,120]; re-cited.

range:sbp:base.item: Systolic BP thresholds th=[120,140] hard-code one guideline frame; no DBP
reasons: Provenance mixed. A single global SBP threshold cannot satisfy direct US/UK divergence: ACC/AHA 2017 (US) defines HTN at >=130; ESC 2023 / NICE NG136 (UK/EU) at >=140 office. Spec's yellow 120/red 140 follows the European/NICE frame and is non-conformant with US ACC/AHA, while sitting alongside US-style lipid/glucose units. No DBP marker exists, so HTN cannot be staged and the age-gate 'J-curve'/frail-elderly relaxation is promised but unwired (frail 78M SBP 142 tips red despite guideline tolerance). Source 'clinical' overstates reliability for a DTC product.
actions: Make SBP cuts jurisdiction/guideline-selectable (2017 ACC/AHA 130 vs 2023 ESC/NICE NG136 140); wire the promised age-band for frail elderly; add a DBP marker; record measurement method.
range:sbp:base.resolution: ≥140/90 cut re-cited from ACC/AHA (which is ≥130/80) to NICE NG136 / ESC 2023 — the convention this value actually follows and which Gulf practice adopts. Values unchanged; citation corrected via apply_range_corrections.py.

range:hba1c:base.item: HbA1c %-only, no IFCC mmol/mol; reliability not cross-gated
reasons: Provenance mixed/US. Cuts 5.7/6.5% are correct ADA values but unit is NGSP %-only with no IFCC mmol/mol path or conversion (5.7%=39, 6.5%=48 mmol/mol). US/UK divergence: US reports NGSP %; UK/EU labs report IFCC mmol/mol as primary since 2011, so a UK value is ~7x larger numerically and would silently mis-band; NICE/WHO also use 6.0% prediabetes boundary vs ADA 5.7%. HbA1c is CRITICAL in MET yet not cross-gated for reliability in anemia/CKD/pregnancy profiles the spec carries; pregnancy frame should use GDM OGTT anchors. UAE: hemoglobinopathy and iron deficiency (both highly prevalent in the Gulf) confound HbA1c, risking population-specific misclassification.
actions: Carry both NGSP % and IFCC mmol/mol with explicit conversion and source-unit detection; expose ADA 5.7% vs NICE/WHO 6.0% as configurable; cross-gate HbA1c validity on anemia/hemoglobinopathy and suppress in pregnancy; cite ADA 2024/2025 and NICE NG28.
range:hba1c:base.resolution: Green moved <5.4→<5.7% (39 mmol/mol) per ADA/WHO; bands carry NGSP% + IFCC mmol/mol; re-cited. Set in pillars/range-variations/calc-graph (th already 5.7,6.5) via apply_range_corrections.py.

gap:lipid-glucose-unit-conversion.item: Per-analyte lipid/glucose unit conversion missing (mg/dL only)
reasons: Provenance US. LDL/HDL/ApoB/TG/glucose are mg/dL only; UK/EU report cholesterol in mmol/L (÷38.67), TG in mmol/L (÷88.57), glucose in mmol/L (÷18.02), and ApoB in g/L in much of the EU. US/UK divergence is analyte-specific, so a single global mg/dL→mmol/L factor would be clinically wrong across analytes. Distinct technical requirement raised by multiple reviewers.
actions: Store per-analyte conversion factors and unit; detect/normalize source unit before banding; never apply one global lipid factor.
gap:lipid-glucose-unit-conversion.resolution: Per-analyte conversions (lin=[m,b]) defined in data/units.json; inbound conversion layer applies before scoring.

range:tg:base.item: Triglycerides red=500 misses atherogenic 200-499 band; CRITICAL trigger mis-set
reasons: Provenance mixed/US. Yellow 150 matches NCEP/ESC borderline but red at 500 only captures pancreatitis-risk severe hypertriglyceridemia; 200-499 (guideline 'high', an ASCVD risk-enhancer per 2018 ACC/AHA and ESC/EAS 2019) reads merely yellow. TG is CRITICAL in MET yet the metsyn profile TG 260 would not fire the MET critical cascade. Unit divergence US mg/dL vs UK/EU mmol/L (150=1.7). UAE: TG is highly distorted by Ramadan-cycle/fasting in a Muslim-majority cohort and by the high-carb South-Asian phenotype; fasting status uncaptured.
actions: Add an intermediate ~200 high-TG band; set the CRITICAL trigger at the pancreatitis level (~880 mg/dL / 10 mmol/L) or reconsider TG as CRITICAL; capture fasting status; add mmol/L; cite 2018 ACC/AHA and ESC/EAS 2019.
range:tg:base.resolution: Invented green <90 removed → NCEP normal <150 (1.7 mmol/L); yellow 150–499 (atherogenic) separated from the ≥500 pancreatitis red; engine th [150,500] retained.

range:egfr:base.item: eGFR unit wrong (mL/min) and equation version unstated
reasons: Provenance mixed/intl. Unit must be mL/min/1.73m2, not mL/min. The CKD-EPI equation version is unstated: US adopted the 2021 race-free equation; legacy race-inclusive or cystatin-C variants differ ~10-16% at the same creatinine, shifting the CRITICAL 60/45 boundary. eGFR is CRITICAL in REN. US/UK divergence: US 2021 CKD-EPI race-free vs legacy/cystatin variants; NICE NG203 and US KDIGO/NKF both use the race-free equation and the eGFR×ACR heat-map. No age-context for benign mildly reduced eGFR in the elderly (frail profile). UAE: equation choice shifts who crosses the critical floor for a mixed South-Asian/Arab cohort.
actions: Fix unit to mL/min/1.73m2; record/specify CKD-EPI 2021 (race-free); use the KDIGO eGFR×UACR matrix rather than eGFR alone; age-context isolated 45-60 in the elderly; cite KDIGO 2024.
range:egfr:base.resolution: G2 (60–89) no longer yellow — green ≥60 (G1–G2), yellow 45–59 (G3a), red <45 (G3b–G5) per KDIGO; unit fixed mL/min→mL/min/1.73m²; engine th [60,45] retained.

range:k:base.item: Potassium one-sided (hi only); hypokalemia invisible despite CRITICAL
reasons: Provenance intl/none. K is CRITICAL in REN but banded one-sided ('hi' only); hypokalemia (<3.5, severe <2.5) is equally arrhythmia-/death-relevant and common with diuretics, yet cannot be flagged (cannot represent K=3.0). Profiles are on ACE inhibitors (raise K) and diuretics (lower K). A CRITICAL marker watching one tail is internally inconsistent. Also K is labile/hemolysis-sensitive. Not a US/UK divergence (mmol/L universal); pure modeling/safety gap.
actions: Make potassium bidirectional (hypo yellow <3.5 / red <3.0 plus existing hyper limb); tie to ACEi/diuretic context; flag hemolysis; cite KDIGO/ERA hyperkalemia guidance.
range:k:base.resolution: Potassium is clinically two-sided (hypo <3.5 / hyper >5.0) but the engine th is one-sided 'hi'. Two-sided support is an engine structural change — scoped, pending sign-off.

range:osa:base.item: OSA AHI thresholds th=[0.5,1] off by an order of magnitude; spurious CRITICAL
reasons: Provenance intl/US. AASM severity is normal <5, mild 5-15, moderate 15-30, severe >=30 events/h; yellow 0.5/red 1 classifies essentially every adult as severe OSA. OSA is CRITICAL in SLP, so this fires R_crit and PURE_CRIT_CAP=40 near-universally — a clear scale/units error (possibly ODI or a 0-1 index mislabeled). US/UK divergence: none (AASM and NICE NG202 both use 5/15/30). Consumer-wearable 'AHI' is also not PSG-validated.
actions: Correct AHI cuts to AASM 5/15/30; verify the metric/source; reconsider the CRITICAL designation for unvalidated wearable estimates; cite AASM 2012/2023.
range:osa:base.resolution: OSA AHI threshold corrected from th=[0.5,1] (off by ~an order of magnitude → spurious criticals) to [5,30] events/h (mild/severe per AASM). Proposed pending sign-off.

range:almi:base.item: ALMI sex-agnostic th=[7,5.5]; female cut applied to all despite CRITICAL
reasons: Provenance EU (EWGSOP2). Sarcopenia ALMI cutpoints are sex-specific: EWGSOP2 M<7.0, F<5.5 kg/m2. The spec collapses both into one 7/5.5 ramp, judging women against a near-male floor (over-flagging) despite an active sex gate. ALMI is CRITICAL in BCM, so a normal woman at ~6.0 could trip the BCM cascade. US/UK divergence: EWGSOP2 (Europe) vs AWGS (Asia) vs FNIH (US) differ. UAE: AWGS values are appropriate for the large South-Asian Gulf population; method (DXA vs BIA) unrecorded.
actions: Sex-resolve ALMI via the sex gate (M<7.0/F<5.5 EWGSOP2); offer AWGS values for the Asian cohort; record DXA vs BIA; note diagnosis needs low strength, not mass alone; cite EWGSOP2 2019.
range:almi:base.resolution: Needs sex/age/menopause-conditioned thresholds and a critical-set redesign (over- and under-inclusive). The sex-gating mechanism exists (Doc 08) but single-value engine th must become conditioned — engine structural work, scoped, pending sign-off.

reasons: Provenance intl. T-score cuts (-1 osteopenia, -2.5 osteoporosis) match WHO but are valid only in postmenopausal women and men >=50; younger adults/premenopausal women require Z-scores (ISCD). Applying T-score CRITICAL to the 28F/33M/35F profiles is population-inappropriate and would mislabel young athletes. Skeletal site unspecified. US/UK divergence: WHO T-score is international, but NICE uses FRAX/QFracture intervention thresholds rather than BMD alone.
actions: Gate T-score CRITICAL to age>=50/postmenopausal; use Z-score otherwise; specify skeletal site; integrate FRAX; cite ISCD 2019 / WHO.
range:tscore:base.resolution: Needs sex/age/menopause-conditioned thresholds and a critical-set redesign (over- and under-inclusive). The sex-gating mechanism exists (Doc 08) but single-value engine th must become conditioned — engine structural work, scoped, pending sign-off.

range:phq:base.item: PHQ-9 th=[5,20] collapses bands and misses item-9 suicidality despite CRITICAL
reasons: Provenance intl/US. Standard PHQ-9 bands are 5/10/15/20; encoding yellow 5/red 20 makes a PHQ-9 of 18 read only yellow. More critically, PHQ-9 safety hinges on item 9 (suicidal ideation), which a total>=20 cut ignores entirely — a person can score <20 yet endorse active SI. PHQ is the sole CRITICAL MCS marker (gad/isi non-critical) and the critical logic targets the wrong quantity; self-report ('pro') also under-reports. US/UK divergence: thresholds are US-origin (Kroenke); NICE contextualises within clinical interview but item-9 safety-netting is universal. UAE: Arabic-version cut-point calibration differs across translations.
actions: Use 5/10/15 graded bands and a dedicated item-9 suicidality safety trigger independent of the total; validate Arabic-version cut-points; re-evaluate GAD/ISI criticality; cite Kroenke PHQ-9 validation / APA.
range:phq:base.resolution: PHQ-9 band collapse + item-9 (suicidality) hard override is a SAFETY gate — routed to the safety layer (Doc 16); pending clinician sign-off, not a silent threshold tweak.

range:waist:base.item: Waist circumference male-only Europid cuts th=[94,102]; no sex/ethnicity gate
reasons: Provenance intl. 94/102 cm are male IDF/WHO Europid cut-points applied to BOTH sexes and ALL ethnicities; female cuts are 80/88 cm, so the 28F/35F/50F profiles are systematically under-flagged despite an active sex gate. IDF mandates ethnicity-specific cuts. US/UK divergence: NICE recommends lower waist/BMI action levels for South Asian/Chinese groups (PH46/NG246); US NCEP ATP III defaults to Europid 102/88 — the spec follows neither. UAE: the Gulf cohort is heavily South-Asian expatriate plus Arab with central adiposity at lower waist (IDF South Asian/Middle Eastern M>=90/F>=80), so 94/102 systematically misses the dominant high-risk lean-waist phenotype.
actions: Sex- AND ethnicity-gate waist (South Asian/Middle Eastern M>=90/F>=80 IDF 2006; at minimum split by sex M 94/102, F 80/88); add inch support; cite IDF 2009 / WHO / NICE.
range:waist:base.resolution: European cuts (94/102) replaced with IDF South-Asian/Gulf cuts (male ≥90, female ≥80) as the cohort default; engine th [94,102]→[90,100]; re-cited IDF 2006.

reasons: Provenance US/intl. Body-fat % healthy ranges are strongly sex-specific (women carry ~8-10% more essential fat); unisex 25/32 mislabels normal female adiposity as high and uses a male-athletic default 18. Source 'clinical' overstates reliability — body fat is usually BIA/wearable/skinfold (high method variance), not a clinical lab (DXA is the reference); method unrecorded. UAE: South Asians carry higher %-fat at a given BMI, relevant to the Gulf and uncaptured. Not a formal US/UK guideline divergence (not a guideline metric).
actions: Sex-gate body-fat bands (men ~25/30, women ~32/38) and ethnicity-adjust for South Asians; record measurement method; downgrade BIA/wearable vs DXA; set sex-appropriate impute defaults; cite ACE/AACE.
range:bodyfat:base.resolution: Needs sex/age/menopause-conditioned thresholds and a critical-set redesign (over- and under-inclusive). The sex-gating mechanism exists (Doc 08) but single-value engine th must become conditioned — engine structural work, scoped, pending sign-off.

range:vo2:base.item: VO2max flat th=[40,30] not age/sex-normed; wearable estimate
reasons: Provenance US/intl. VO2max norms are strongly age- and sex-dependent (40 mL/kg/min is excellent at 70, average at 25); a flat 40/30 ramp mislabels older and female users as low-fitness and over-rewards young men. The age gate text promises 'age-normed fitness' that is unwired. Source is wearable-estimated (e.g., pace+HR), imprecise and invalid on HR-altering meds — the post-MI profile on C07AB (beta-blocker) with VO2 34 is a concrete invalidation case. No formal US/UK divergence (both use age/sex percentile tables).
actions: Replace the flat band with sex×age percentile norms (ACSM/Cooper/FRIEND) as the age gate promises; flag beta-blocker invalidation; mark wearable estimate lower confidence.
range:vo2:base.resolution: Needs sex/age/menopause-conditioned thresholds and a critical-set redesign (over- and under-inclusive). The sex-gating mechanism exists (Doc 08) but single-value engine th must become conditioned — engine structural work, scoped, pending sign-off.

range:hb:base.item: Hemoglobin sex/pregnancy-agnostic th=[13,10] and g/dL-only; CRITICAL
reasons: Provenance US/intl. WHO anemia cuts are sex-specific (M<13, non-pregnant F<12, pregnant F<11); unisex 13 under-flags men's deeper bands and over-flags women, and the pregnancy profile (Hb 11.5, normal-physiologic) scores red. Hb is CRITICAL in HEM. US/UK divergence: unit g/dL (US) vs g/L (UK/EU, x10; 13=130 g/L) is a silent garbage-value hazard on a CRITICAL marker. UAE: high Gulf consanguinity drives very high beta/alpha-thalassaemia prevalence (UAE premarital screening); trait carriers run chronically low Hb with normal iron and would misclassify as a CRITICAL hematologic red, firing R_crit and PURE_CRIT_CAP=40 — a population-specific false-positive cascade.
actions: Sex- and pregnancy-resolve Hb cuts via gates (M13/F12/preg11 WHO); encode g/L conversion; add a hemoglobinopathy gate (UAE premarital screen) routing trait carriers to MCV/HbA2 context rather than the CRITICAL cascade; cite WHO 2011/2024.
range:hb:base.resolution: Needs sex/age/menopause-conditioned thresholds and a critical-set redesign (over- and under-inclusive). The sex-gating mechanism exists (Doc 08) but single-value engine th must become conditioned — engine structural work, scoped, pending sign-off.

const:PURE_CRIT_CAP.item: PURE_CRIT_CAP=40 flat cap collapses all critical states
reasons: Provenance none (engine knob). A single global hard cap of 40 collapses every critical state to the same ceiling regardless of severity or which pillar fired (transient CRP>10 and a true K+ 6.5 / Hb 8 emergency both cap at 40), destroying discrimination. Combined with over-broad CRITICAL designations and several mis-set thresholds (OSA AHI=1, unisex Hb, wearable SpO2, male-only waist), the cap fires spuriously and frequently, eroding clinical trust. Cited only to 'Doc 03 §5' with no calibration rationale. No US/UK divergence. UAE: population-mis-specified criticals (thalassaemia Hb, ALMI sex, vitD impute) make spurious firing worse for a Gulf cohort.
actions: Tier the cap by criticality/number of critical pillars and gate it on measurement confidence; first fix the over-broad CRITICAL set so the cap is meaningful; justify/calibrate against outcome data.
const:PURE_CRIT_CAP.resolution: constants.json now declares calibration_status=expert-prior + per-symbol basis; each flagged constant (R_crit confidence-scaling, flat PURE_CRIT_CAP, q_impute/Rp_impute on criticals, cov_green_floor, NHANES/UK-Biobank-only r_cohort) is tagged for cohort calibration with ethnicity/region strata. Values unchanged pending sign-off.

critical:set.item: CRITICAL designation set simultaneously over-inclusive and under-protective
reasons: Provenance none (engine config). The CRITICAL array includes measurement-noisy wearable SpO2 and erroneous OSA AHI@1 (over-inclusive) while electrolytes are one-sided (K hyper-only, hypokalemia missed) and acute tripwires are absent (no eGFR<15/dialysis-range, no sodium, no troponin/acute-MI, no DBP), and TG is critical at the wrong cut — under-protective. plt/alt/ldl as binary critical ignore severity/context. No US/UK divergence. UAE: noisy wearable criticals plus population-mis-specified thresholds amplify false firing for the Gulf cohort.
actions: Re-derive the CRITICAL set from outcome severity; exclude noisy wearable-only signals from hard caps; make electrolytes bidirectional; add missing acute cardiac/renal-failure/sodium tripwires.
critical:set.resolution: Needs sex/age/menopause-conditioned thresholds and a critical-set redesign (over- and under-inclusive). The sex-gating mechanism exists (Doc 08) but single-value engine th must become conditioned — engine structural work, scoped, pending sign-off.

const:q_impute.item: Cohort imputation of CRITICAL markers (q_impute=0.30, Rp_impute=0.70)
reasons: Provenance none/mixed. Imputing missing labs to an age×sex×life-stage cohort MEDIAN at confidence 0.30 then scoring is clinically hazardous for CRITICAL markers: a patient with no measured potassium/eGFR/LDL/Hb is assigned a normal-ish median, masking true abnormality on a score-capping pathway. Rp_impute=0.70 is a single global representativeness number that cannot be right across markers/populations. US/UK divergence: NHANES (US) and UK-Biobank (UK) cohorts differ in ancestry/age structure and the blend basis is unstated. UAE: the cohort match has no ethnicity/region dimension, so imputing vitD/Hb/waist to a Western median is biased for a Gulf cohort and Rp=0.70 is overstated.
actions: Never impute CRITICAL markers — show as missing/unknown; make Rp_impute marker/population-specific; add ethnicity/region as a cohort-matching dimension; source Gulf-specific reference distributions; justify the 0.30/0.70 values.
const:q_impute.resolution: constants.json now declares calibration_status=expert-prior + per-symbol basis; each flagged constant (R_crit confidence-scaling, flat PURE_CRIT_CAP, q_impute/Rp_impute on criticals, cov_green_floor, NHANES/UK-Biobank-only r_cohort) is tagged for cohort calibration with ethnicity/region strata. Values unchanged pending sign-off.

gap:missing-cv-renal-markers.item: GAP: no DBP, Lp(a), non-HDL-C, sodium, or acute cardiac marker
reasons: Provenance mixed/intl. For a CV/MET/REN-heavy engine, several guideline-recommended markers are absent: diastolic BP (HTN staging and the age-gate J-curve frame need it), Lp(a) (ESC/EAS 2022 once-in-lifetime), non-HDL-C, serum sodium (core electrolyte safety signal alongside K), and any acute troponin/symptom tripwire. US/UK divergence: non-HDL-C is the primary NICE (UK) lipid target whereas the US emphasizes LDL/ApoB. Their absence limits guideline conformance and safety coverage.
actions: Add DBP, non-HDL-C/Lp(a), and sodium markers; define an acute-symptom escalation path; cite ESC/EAS 2022 Lp(a), NICE lipid, ACC/AHA HTN.
gap:missing-cv-renal-markers.resolution: Logged in data/coverage.json (markers): DBP, Lp(a), non-HDL-C, sodium, free T4 + fasting/method fields scoped with a concrete add/derive plan, rendered on production-gaps.html. Engine implementation pending sign-off.

reasons: Provenance US. Low-HDL risk cutoffs are sex-specific (M<40, F<50 per NCEP/AHA metabolic-syndrome criteria); the single 50/40 ramp uses the female yellow and male red, mislabeling both sexes despite an active sex gate (penalises healthy men 42-49 into yellow). Very high HDL (>90) paradoxical risk uncaptured. US/UK divergence: unit mg/dL (US) vs mmol/L (UK/EU); NICE de-emphasises HDL targets in favour of non-HDL/QRISK, so a single cut matches neither.
actions: Sex-gate HDL cuts (M<40, F<50); add mmol/L; document source; cite NCEP ATP-III / IDF metabolic-syndrome.

critical:crp.item: hsCRP th=[1,10] conflates CV bands with acute-phase; CRITICAL mis-assigned
reasons: Provenance US/intl. hsCRP CV-risk bands are <1/1-3/>3 mg/L (AHA/CDC 2003); 10 mg/L is acute infection territory, so red at 10 (and yellow at 1 not 3) conflates acute-phase response with CV risk. CRP is CRITICAL in INF, so any intercurrent infection/vaccination/injury transiently spikes it and fires R_crit, generating frequent false criticals, while chronic low-grade inflammation (metsyn 3.5) never fires; WBC in the same pillar is non-critical — inconsistent. US/UK divergence: AHA/CDC use 1/3 tertiles; NICE does not endorse hsCRP for routine CV risk, so 1/10 matches neither.
actions: Separate hsCRP CV-risk tertiles (1/3) from acute CRP; demote hsCRP from CRITICAL (treat >10 as recheck/acute flag) or require persistence before firing the cascade; cite AHA/CDC 2003.
critical:crp.resolution: Needs sex/age/menopause-conditioned thresholds and a critical-set redesign (over- and under-inclusive). The sex-gating mechanism exists (Doc 08) but single-value engine th must become conditioned — engine structural work, scoped, pending sign-off.

range:tsh:base.item: TSH one-sided (hi only); no age/pregnancy ranges
reasons: Provenance US/intl. One-sided 'hi' cannot flag suppressed TSH (<0.4, hyperthyroidism with AF/thyroid-storm risk) — a dangerous-low-tail blind spot. No age-adjustment (ATA: upper reference rises with age, >=7-8 may be normal in the elderly) and no trimester-specific ranges despite a pregnancy gate/profile (31F). US/UK divergence: ATA (US) trimester-specific TSH; NICE NG145 lab/age-specific ranges — both two-sided, spec is one-sided.
actions: Add a low-TSH (hyperthyroid) limb; apply trimester-specific ranges under the pregnancy gate; age-adjust the elderly upper limit; cite ATA 2017.
range:tsh:base.resolution: Abandoned narrow 0.5–2.5 green widened to ATA 0.4–4.0; suppressed <0.3 retained as red; re-cited. Age/pregnancy trimester ranges noted for a follow-up variation.

range:fib4:base.item: FIB-4 low cutoff 1.3 not age-adjusted for >=65
reasons: Provenance US. Cuts 1.3/2.67 are the standard dual-cutoff but validated for ages 35-65; in adults >=65 the low cutoff should rise to 2.0 to avoid false positives (AASLD 2023 MASLD). FIB-4 is CRITICAL and the 78yo frail profile carries hepatic markers, so a flat 1.3 over-flags the elderly. No specific US/UK divergence noted; AASLD/EASL concordant on age-adjustment.
actions: Age-adjust the FIB-4 low cutoff to 2.0 for >=65; cite AASLD 2023 MASLD guidance / EASL.
range:fib4:base.resolution: Needs sex/age/menopause-conditioned thresholds and a critical-set redesign (over- and under-inclusive). The sex-gating mechanism exists (Doc 08) but single-value engine th must become conditioned — engine structural work, scoped, pending sign-off.

selfreport:rhr-hrv.item: Resting HR / HRV scored with fixed population cuts despite wearable variance
reasons: Provenance intl. RHR (th 70/85) and HRV/rMSSD (40/25 ms) are wearable-derived but run through the same fixed-threshold machinery as labs. Wearable RHR/HRV are device-, algorithm-, and posture-dependent (optical PPG vs ECG chest strap differ materially) with large night-to-night variance; rMSSD absolute values are not comparable across vendors and are only meaningful as a personal trend. Measurement-method validity is not encoded beyond q_source=0.8. No US/UK divergence.
actions: Score wearable RHR/HRV as personal-baseline deviations (z vs own baseline) rather than fixed population cuts; record device class; gate on baseline data sufficiency.
selfreport:rhr-hrv.resolution: Wearable/self-report variance nuance; scoped for the confidence-model pass.

reasons: Provenance none. The cohort match is age×sex×life-stage with NO ethnicity/region dimension — the core population-validity flaw for a Gulf deployment. Imputing vitamin D, ferritin/Hb, waist, body-fat, and lipids to a Western NHANES/UK-Biobank-derived median biases toward the wrong reference (e.g., vitD imputed to 40 ng/mL). Rp_impute=0.70 asserts 70% representativeness, overstated with no ethnicity dimension for South-Asian/Arab users; the cited cohorts contain few Gulf residents. US/UK divergence: cohort sources are US (NHANES) / UK (UK-Biobank), neither representing a Gulf cohort. UAE: this is the enabling population defect.
actions: Add ethnicity/region as a cohort-matching dimension; source Gulf-specific reference distributions; lower Rp_impute when no regional match exists; state the cohort source and its Gulf representativeness.

range:vitd:default.item: Vitamin D impute default 40 ng/mL implausible for Gulf cohort
reasons: Provenance UAE. The impute/cohort-median default of 40 ng/mL is implausible for a Gulf cohort, where 50-90% are <20 ng/mL (clothing, indoor lifestyle, pigmentation despite sunshine). Imputing missing vitamin D to 40 tells deficient Gulf users they are replete — a population-inappropriate optimistic default masking near-universal regional deficiency. The 30/20 thresholds themselves are defensible; the impute default is the error. US/UK divergence: US Endocrine Society sufficiency >=30 ng/mL vs UK SACN/NICE far more conservative (~25 nmol/L floor); spec uses US-style ng/mL.
actions: Set the Gulf age×sex×region cohort median far lower (literature often <15-20 ng/mL); ideally make vitamin D non-imputable for this cohort to force measurement; add nmol/L.
range:vitd:default.resolution: Aggressive US ≥30 floor replaced with IOM/SACN sufficiency ≥20 ng/mL (50 nmol/L); nmol/L path added; engine th [30,20]→[20,12], impute default 40→20 (Gulf-plausible); re-cited.

reasons: Provenance UAE. G6PD deficiency is X-linked and highly prevalent in the Gulf/Middle East (consanguinity plus Mediterranean/Asian haplotypes; UAE national newborn/premarital screening). It is material to a scoring+NUDGE engine: it contraindicates common nudges (high-dose vitamin C, fava beans, certain supplements) and causes episodic hemolytic anemia (transient low Hb that spuriously trips the HEM CRITICAL cascade). No G6PD attribute, gate, or nudge-safety interlock exists. US/UK divergence: neither ACC/AHA nor NICE centre G6PD (low Western prevalence) — exactly a region-specific gap the source frameworks would not surface.
actions: Add a G6PD-status gate (from premarital/newborn screen) that suppresses contraindicated nudges and contextualises episodic Hb drops so they do not fire R_crit.

gap:dbp-marker.item: GAP: no diastolic blood pressure marker
reasons: Provenance intl/mixed. Only systolic BP is captured. Isolated diastolic hypertension and wide/narrow pulse pressure carry independent risk; HTN cannot be staged nor the age-gate J-curve frame applied without DBP. ESC/ACC define HTN on both SBP and DBP. A BP-driven CV/REN engine without DBP is clinically under-specified. US/UK divergence: both ACC/AHA (130/80) and NICE/ESC (140/90) require the diastolic component.
actions: Add a dbp marker feeding the BP/CV pathway with paired SBP/DBP banding.
gap:dbp-marker.resolution: Logged in data/coverage.json (markers): DBP, Lp(a), non-HDL-C, sodium, free T4 + fasting/method fields scoped with a concrete add/derive plan, rendered on production-gaps.html. Engine implementation pending sign-off.

gap:lipid-fasting-method-lpa.item: GAP: lipid panel lacks fasting status / LDL method; no Lp(a)
reasons: Provenance mixed. ApoB/LDL/TG are scored without fasting status (TG is fasting-sensitive; the 150/500 cut assumes fasting) or LDL method — calculated Friedewald LDL is invalid at TG>400, exactly the spec's TG red zone, so LDL is unreliable precisely when TG is critical. There is also no Lp(a), an independent largely-genetic ASCVD factor now guideline-recommended once-in-lifetime (ESC/EAS 2022). UAE: relevant to the high-TG South-Asian phenotype where Friedewald LDL underperforms.
actions: Capture fasting status and LDL method (direct vs calculated); add an Lp(a) once-in-lifetime marker; cite ESC/EAS 2022 Lp(a).

coupling:hba1c<-hb.item: HbA1c validity not cross-gated on hemoglobinopathy/anemia despite CRITICAL
reasons: Provenance intl. HbA1c is invalidated by hemoglobinopathies, recent transfusion, and altered RBC turnover (the frail/anemic profiles 7,8 have low Hb), yet is scored at full lab authority and is CRITICAL in MET. In iron deficiency or hemolysis HbA1c is unreliable; the spec collects ferritin/Hb but does not cross-gate. UAE: thalassaemia and iron deficiency are both highly prevalent in the Gulf, so this measurement-validity interaction is population-critical. Distinct from the unit finding.
actions: Cross-gate HbA1c validity on anemia/hemoglobinopathy flags (using collected Hb/ferritin); fall back to fasting glucose/fructosamine when invalid.
coupling:hba1c<-hb.resolution: HbA1c reliability gate specified: in haemoglobinopathy/anaemia/CKD/pregnancy prefer fructosamine/fasting glucose before HbA1c floors MET (critical). Gulf G6PD/thalassaemia prevalence flagged — pending clinician sign-off.

const:R_crit.item: R_crit=0.60 + cap fire on low-confidence imputed/wearable criticals
reasons: Provenance none. The CRITICAL cascade interacts badly with population-mis-specified thresholds: because many CRITICAL markers use wrong/sex-agnostic cuts (Hb/thalassaemia, ALMI sex, OSA scale error, one-sided K, vitD impute), R_crit=0.60 plus the hard PURE_CRIT_CAP=40 fires frequently on false positives, and a single global floor with no confidence weighting lets a low-confidence imputed or wearable critical cap the whole score. No justification given for 0.60. No US/UK divergence (internal engine parameter). UAE: amplified for the Gulf cohort by the population-specific false positives.
actions: Gate the CRITICAL cascade on measurement confidence (do not let imputed/low-q-source criticals fire R_crit); require persistence/confirmation for state-dependent markers; fix the underlying population specs; justify 0.60 empirically.

const:cov_green_floor.item: cov_green_floor=0.60 allows green without critical-marker coverage
reasons: Provenance none. cov_green_floor=0.60 lets a pillar display green on just 60% marker coverage, but if the missing 40% are the critical apob/ldl, a green CV with no atherogenic data is misleading. ρ_k=0.20 is an uncited magic number (Doc 03 §3). The coverage floor should interact with WHICH markers are missing (especially criticals), not raw fraction. No US/UK divergence (internal design).
actions: Make green eligibility require critical-marker coverage, not just >=0.60 overall; justify ρ_k and cov_green_floor.
